phases.name: Walking skeleton — Vmm port, VmDriver, DriverRegistry, an honest exit code (Slice 01)

steps.name: Vmm port trait + VmConfig anti-corruption value family
steps.description: Land the Vmm port trait signature and VmConfig's pure value family (DiskAttachment, VmRunDir, MemoryPlan, KernelImage, VmConfinement) that make three substrate lies structurally discouraged and lint-enforced (ADR-0082 D1/D2).
criteria: VmConfinement::seccomp_arg() renders the literal "true" unconditionally; no code path can render "false" or "log".
DiskAttachment::to_disk_arg() always emits image_type=raw for every path/read_only combination, at one rendering site.
KernelImage::validate(path, arch, header) is pure, rejects a non-matching magic before any I/O, and accepts x86_64 bzImage/PVH vmlinux and aarch64 raw PE Image.
MemoryPlan::derive(declared) is the only constructor; guest_bytes() and cgroup_max_bytes() can never be equal.
reserve_bytes(guest_bytes) ships as a todo!("RED scaffold") citing the memory.current/memory.stat measurement it needs, never a guessed constant.
steps.implementation_notes: TEST PARADIGM: Tier 1, default lane, pure functions — proptest over the domain of each (any VmConfinement value; any path/read_only pair; any header byte window; any declared u64). UNSKIP FOUR of the five existing RED scaffolds (#[should_panic(expected="RED scaffold")]) in vm_config_pure_functions.rs — S-VM-08 (seccomp), S-VM-16 (disk), S-VM-17 (kernel format), S-VM-18 (MemoryPlan invariant) — replacing each panic body with a proptest! block per ADR-0082 §D2.1-D2.5's pinned signatures; do not invent a different constructor or field (CLAUDE.md 'Implement to the design'). MemoryPlan/KernelImage/DiskAttachment/VmConfinement are all mandatory mutation targets (brief.md §113) — run cargo xtask mutants --file against each after GREEN. S-VM-20 (reserve_bytes) is the FIFTH scaffold and stays RED here — do NOT unskip it and do NOT write a guessed constant; reserve_bytes(guest_bytes) ships as a todo!() body citing the memory.current/memory.stat measurement it needs. Its scaffold is unskipped, its body written, its @mandatory:mutation_target tag added, and its scoped mutation gate run in ONE LATER commit — step 01-05 — not here (§D2.3, brief §113). (Corrects a prior-draft contradiction that claimed all five scaffolds unskip in this step while simultaneously keeping reserve_bytes a todo!().)

Read the existing workload_intent.rs file FIRST (DWD-06 point 5) before editing — FIXTURE_V1 is NEVER touched, only appended to. Follow development.md 'rkyv schema evolution' → 'Version-bump procedure' steps 1-6 in a single commit.

steps.name: overdrive-init guest agent crate + beacon Published Language
steps.description: New static-musl binary crate: PID 1 in the guest, beacons READY once, execs the operator's command, reports the real WEXITSTATUS over vsock, reads at most one SHUTDOWN.
criteria: overdrive-init is a new crate_class="binary" crate, built static for {x86_64,aarch64}-unknown-linux-musl, both targets wired into the toolchain and CI.
The beacon wire protocol (READY/EXIT/SHUTDOWN/EOF) lives once in overdrive_core::vm::beacon, consumed by both host and guest — no second parser.
overdrive-init execs the operator's command, forwards stdio, and reports the real exit status; it never validates the operator's own I/O.
A round-trip proptest on the beacon parser/formatter passes for arbitrary READY/EXIT payloads.
steps.scenario_name: S-VM-01 (guest-side prerequisite; the Tier-3 assertion lands in step 01-08)
steps.implementation_notes: TEST PARADIGM: Tier 1, default lane, proptest over the beacon parser (newtype-roundtrip discipline, testing.md). No DISTILL scenario names this crate directly — it is the prerequisite S-VM-01 needs; author this test fresh (DWD-06a: crafter authors RED scaffolds outside the 15 DISTILL committed). Per ADR-0082 §D7: line-oriented ASCII, TWO distinct reads for READY and EXIT (never parsed out of one blob). No publish pipeline (GH #259 owns the OCI/Dockerfile→rootfs factory that injects this binary) — this step's whole obligation is the crate + the two build targets.

steps.name: Real-boot fixture provisioning — pinned kernel + ext4 rootfs + overdrive-init, staged for Tier-3 VM tests
steps.description: Land the fixture helper vm_walking_skeleton.rs's real bodies (and every later Tier-3 VM scenario in Slices 01-05) call: stage a pinned kernel and ext4 rootfs with overdrive-init baked in at its well-known path on a reflink-capable directory, confirm cloud-hypervisor is installed, and fail loudly when any prerequisite is missing. This is Slice 01's own first sub-step (brief.md 'Handoff to DELIVER' item 1) — none of it exists in the tree yet, per the committed scaffold's own note (vm_walking_skeleton.rs:22-28).
criteria: The fixture helper stages a pinned kernel image and an ext4 rootfs image, with the overdrive-init binary (crate overdrive-init, step 01-03) baked into the rootfs at its well-known path, on a directory confirmed reflink-capable by a real FICLONE probe (never an fstype string comparison, per C-1).

cloud-hypervisor is confirmed present and its version floor checked before any test proceeds; a missing or too-old binary fails fixture setup with a named, actionable error rather than surfacing as a downstream test timeout.
The fixture is the single provisioning surface every Tier-3 VM test in this feature (Slices 01-05) calls — no test hand-stages its own kernel, rootfs, or cloud-hypervisor check.

The fixture is idempotent and safely re-runnable across repeated Lima test invocations — a second call reuses or re-verifies the staged artifacts rather than re-downloading/re-baking from scratch on every run.
steps.scenario_name: Prerequisite for S-VM-01 and every Tier-3 VM scenario in this feature (brief.md 'Handoff to DELIVER' item 1; committed scaffold crates/overdrive-cli/tests/integration/vm_walking_skeleton.rs:22-28, which names this exact gap)
steps.implementation_notes: TEST PARADIGM: real-infra shared test fixture (development.md § 'Shared real-infra test fixtures — overdrive-testing') — dev-dependency only, never [dependencies], per that section's placement rule; consumed by every Tier-3 VM test crate across Slices 01-05, which is exactly the ≥2-crate / non-trivial-setup promotion criteria that section names. Run under cargo xtask lima run -- as root (real cgroup/kernel/CH boot envelope, testing.md § 'Running tests — Lima VM'). This step has NO ADR-pinned signature — DELIVER names the fixture helper's exact API at RED phase; there is no design artifact to diverge from here, unlike the ADR-pinned VmConfig/Vmm surfaces elsewhere in this slice. Kernel/rootfs staging here is TEST-envelope provisioning (Lima), distinct from the production appliance image DEVOPS owns (brief §114's infra/metal/provision.sh handoff annotation) — this step does not touch infra/.

steps.name: reserve_bytes — real-boot memory.current/memory.stat measurement
steps.description: Measure the VM cgroup memory reserve against a real Cloud Hypervisor boot (memory.current / memory.stat, never RSS — host page tables for the guest mapping are charged to the scope and invisible to RSS), give reserve_bytes(guest_bytes) a real body citing the measurement in its own docstring, and close S-VM-20's deferred mutation obligation in the same commit. MemoryPlan::derive is the only VmConfig.memory constructor, so cgroup_max_bytes() sits on the production path of every VM boot (brief.md §102) — this is the hardest DELIVER dependency the design creates, and every later step that constructs a real VmConfig depends on it.
criteria: reserve_bytes(guest_bytes) returns a value derived from a real-boot memory.current/memory.stat measurement (never RSS) against the fixture from step 01-04, with the measured figures cited by name in the function's own docstring, replacing the todo!() RED scaffold.

S-VM-20's scaffold in vm_config_pure_functions.rs is unskipped into a real proptest asserting the returned value is >= 0 and <= a documented upper bound (a fraction of guest_bytes plus a fixed floor, both named in the docstring), for any guest_bytes value.
S-VM-20 gains the @mandatory:mutation_target tag in the SAME commit that gives reserve_bytes its body (brief §113 — a todo!() body has nothing to mutate, so the tag could not attach at step 01-01).
cargo xtask mutants --file crates/overdrive-core/src/vm/config.rs (scoped to reserve_bytes) is run and its kill-rate gate passes before this step closes.

MemoryPlan::derive(declared) now produces a cgroup_max_bytes() bounded by the measured reserve for any declared guest RAM figure; every later step that constructs a real VmConfig (the Vmm adapters, VmDriver, the walking skeleton, and every Tier-3 scenario in Slices 02-05) no longer panics on this path.
steps.implementation_notes: TEST PARADIGM: Tier 1, default lane, proptest for the unskipped S-VM-20 scaffold (bounds check against the documented upper bound) — the MEASUREMENT itself is a one-off real-boot exercise under cargo xtask lima run -- (real cloud-hypervisor + the 01-04 fixture, memory.current/memory.stat read directly off the allocation's cgroup, never RSS), not a permanent test; the docstring citation is the durable artifact (brief §102, ADR-0082 §D2.3). Measure BEFORE writing the body — a guessed constant between the two RSS-derived floors (~5.4 MiB steady-state, ~11.9 MiB pre-residency) is intake precedent #7's 'magic version floor' failure repeated with different units (brief §102). This step does NOT require the CloudHypervisorVmm Rust adapter (step 01-06) to be complete — the measurement drives cloud-hypervisor directly against the 01-04 fixture; it is placed before the Vmm adapter and VmDriver steps precisely so THEIR construction of a real VmConfig via MemoryPlan::derive does not itself panic on the still-todo!() reserve_bytes.

steps.name: CloudHypervisorVmm + SimVmm adapters — probe, create, terminate
steps.description: The two Vmm port implementors: real spawn/FICLONE/argv-render against cloud-hypervisor, and the DST double. Enforced by a two-adapter equivalence test.
criteria: Both adapters produce observably equivalent outcomes across probe/create/terminate, including the six pinned edge cases (ADR-0082 §D6).
create() clones the rootfs via the FICLONE ioctl on the master's own filesystem, never cp; on a real non-reflink target it returns a typed errno, no full-copy fallback, no VMM spawned.
create() removes its clone if the spawn fails; a stale clone destination from a prior crash is replaced, not adopted untouched.
terminate() on an already-dead VMM returns Ok(Killed); probe() is idempotent and leaves no residue.
steps.implementation_notes: TEST PARADIGM: Tier 3, gated integration-tests, single-example call-sequence per Mandate 9 (@example, not @property — a fixed hand-enumerated sequence, not generated input). Run via cargo xtask lima run --. S-VM-94 (vmm_ficlone_per_launch.rs) needs a REAL non-reflink fixture (tmpfs TempDir or loopback ext4), no SimVmm. Mandatory mutation target: the FICLONE call must be killed by a mutant substituting a full-copy fallback. Depends on the 01-04 fixture (real cloud-hypervisor + rootfs to spawn/clone against) and 01-05 (reserve_bytes must have a real body before any test here constructs a full VmConfig via MemoryPlan::derive — every VmConfig.memory field is mandatory).

steps.name: VmDriver — cgroup/netns placement, three-way boot race, authorship claim, stop totality
steps.description: Driver over Arc<dyn Vmm>: takes the supervision claim at step 0, races beacon/exit/deadline (biased), classifies exit from the guest report only, and is total over VmDriver::stop's four edge sequences.
criteria: VmDriver::start takes the supervision claim before the run directory exists; every non-Ok race arm releases it and cleans up the scope/dir/clone/VMM.
A guest EXIT report over vsock is drained and read to completion before the ExitEvent is emitted; the VMM's own subsequent teardown exit never overwrites it.
VmDriver::stop lands Terminated/Stopped{Operator} across all four sequences: pre-beacon stop, unresponsive guest, already-dead VMM, double-stop — never a crash.
Driver gains two defaulted sync methods, live_allocations() and release_supervision(); VmDriver overrides both, ExecDriver keeps the no-op defaults.
steps.implementation_notes: TEST PARADIGM: component-scope, default lane, example-only per Mandate 9 (four FIXED hand-enumerated call sequences against SimVmm, not generated input — @example). Author this RED scaffold fresh (new file, not one of the 15 committed by DISTILL); driving port and edge cases are pinned verbatim in ADR-0082 §D3/§D4 — do not improvise the race shape or the VM_SHUTDOWN_REQUEST_DEADLINE/VM_STOP_GRACE constants (2s/10s). VmExitWatch::recv MUST take &mut self, never self (ADR-0082 §D3 correction). No code path may derive ExitKind from cloud-hypervisor's own exit status — mandatory mutation target, alongside the three race arms' cleanup paths (brief §113 — a mutation dropping cleanup on any non-Ok arm must be killed). S-VM-14 (deadline-arm leak) and S-VM-15 (EXIT-report priority) are AC-06's Tier-3/@real-io evidence for this same race and cleanup logic — DWD-04 commits them to overdrive-cli/tests/integration (real CH, real in-process serve), which does not exist until the walking skeleton lands; their real-boot proof is step 01-08, not here. This step's own SimVmm-driven tests (S-VM-76 plus crafter-authored race-arm examples grounded in ADR-0082 §D3/§D4) are the component-scope RED/GREEN evidence; do not rewrite S-VM-14/15 into SimVmm shadows to close them here — that is the testing theatre DISTILL rejected at S-VM-75's own precedent.

steps.name: DriverRegistry + composition root + spec-parse dispatch + the five-seam wiring
steps.description: Replace AppState.driver with DriverRegistry; discover→probe→insert cloud-hypervisor; route dispatch/exit_observer/ServerHandle/MtlsInterceptWorker through it; parser accepts exactly one driver table.
criteria: overdrive serve composes DriverRegistry (discover→probe→insert); a real [vm]+[job] deploy boots a real Cloud Hypervisor VM and reports the guest's exit code, never the VMM's.
Exactly one of [exec]/[vm] is required; both present or neither is rejected, naming both tables, no allocation created.
Running is reported only after the ready beacon; a rootfs with no working init reaches Failed without ever passing through Running.
MtlsInterceptWorker installs are gated on DriverType::Exec at both call sites; an mTLS-composed VM allocation gets no bound listener and no installed TPROXY rule.
exit_observer runs one task per registry entry; ServerHandle holds Vec<JoinHandle>, cancels once and awaits all on shutdown; alloc_drivers routes stop/terminal arms.

The deadline arm of the three-way boot race leaks nothing: a guest that never beacons ready reaches Failed with no cloud-hypervisor process, run directory, rootfs clone, or cgroup scope remaining for that allocation, and its supervision claim (taken at step 0 of start) released (S-VM-14).

A guest EXIT report over vsock is never overwritten by the VMM's own subsequent teardown exit — the reported exit code stays the guest's, with the report's arrival ordered strictly before the ExitEvent emission (S-VM-15).
steps.implementation_notes: TEST PARADIGM: walking-skeleton Tier 3 (real serve+deploy, real cloud-hypervisor, real guest kernel — the ONLY scenario group in this feature with a real guest kernel), gated integration-tests, single-example (Mandate 9 layer 3+). UNSKIP the 5 vm_walking_skeleton.rs scaffolds (S-VM-01..05) AND the 2 vm_spec_driver_table_dispatch.rs scaffolds (S-VM-06/07) — replace panic bodies with real assertions, real fixture (step 01-04). Author S-VM-74 fresh in the same file (extends the walking skeleton, DWD-04 addendum). Pin AllocationSpec.driver: DriverPayload and action_shim::dispatch's signature EXACTLY as ADR-0083 §D2a/§D3 — do not invent a different index shape for alloc_drivers. The parser's driver-table dispatch (exactly-one-of-[exec]/[vm]) is a mandatory mutation target (brief §113) — a mutant that admits both-or-neither tables must be killed. GH #248/ADR-0074 trap: S-VM-05 MUST run against an mTLS-composed serve (dataplane_override unset). S-VM-14/S-VM-15 (AC-06, @tier3 @real-io) join this step per DWD-04's crate placement (overdrive-cli/tests/integration) — VmDriver's own component-scope suite (SimVmm, step 01-07) cannot supply real-CH evidence for the deadline-arm cleanup or the EXIT-report priority; this is the first step with both a real fixture (01-04) and a real DriverRegistry-composed serve, so it is their correct home, not 01-07.

steps.name: Composition-gate fault injection (vmm_override seam) + CgroupAccounting OOM diagnosis
steps.description: ServerConfig.vmm_override wires SimVmm's fault-injection into a real serve boot; CgroupAccounting closes the D-3 fold-in so a wrong reserve_bytes is diagnosed VmOutOfMemory, never a bare signal 9.
criteria: CH present and healthy composes the Vm driver entry; CH absent boots the node with no Vm entry and rejects [vm] at admission naming the capability.
A capability-flag probe failure (Landlock flag/LSM absent, /dev/kvm unreachable) refuses the boot with health.startup.refused, injected via ServerConfig.vmm_override.
A real non-reflink staging directory refuses the boot via an executed FICLONE ioctl, never an fstype string comparison.

A VM whose memory.max is deliberately undersized is classified Failed/VmOutOfMemory{limit_bytes,oom_kill_count}, never WorkloadCrashedImmediately{signal:9}; disposition StoppedBy::Process, restart budget consumed as any crash.
steps.implementation_notes: TEST PARADIGM: Tier 3, gated integration-tests, single-example. ServerConfig.vmm_override: Option<Arc<dyn Vmm>>, #[cfg(feature="integration-tests")]-gated on both the field and its one use site — mirrors mtls_identity_override, NOT dataplane_override (ADR-0083 §D8). probe() runs unconditionally regardless of which adapter is bound. CgroupAccounting is a NEW port beside CgroupFs, not a widening of it (ADR-0083 §A8 already rejected that). S-VM-93 (cgroup_accounting_equivalence.rs) covers the 3-row probe fault table (Substrate/SubstrateCorrupt/MissingOomKillKey). Mandatory mutation target: exit_observer's new precedence check.

steps.name: dst-lint enforcement clauses + per-thread seccomp + DriverType::MicroVm deletion
steps.description: Static AST-scanner clauses closing the lint half of §102's ACL claim; the runtime per-thread seccomp guard; single-cut deletion of the dead MicroVm variant.
criteria: dst-lint rejects a "--disk" / "--landlock-rules" / "--seccomp" string literal outside its one named rendering function, and a MemoryPlan struct literal outside overdrive-core.
Seccomp is verified by reading /proc/<vmm-pid>/task/*/status for the vmm/http-server/vcpu0 threads; a bare /proc/<vmm-pid>/status read alone is never the sole evidence.
DriverType::MicroVm is deleted, OpenAPI is regenerated, and the stale "wire form never changes" docstring is corrected — same PR.
SimVmm is reachable from a Tier-1 DST run (cargo dst).
steps.implementation_notes: TEST PARADIGM (dst-lint clauses): EXEMPT FROM PARADIGM — static-analysis AST-scanner unit tests in xtask (excluded from mutation testing per project convention), following the existing CrashObservabilityStructLiteral clause shape verbatim; not a property over program behavior. TEST PARADIGM (S-VM-09): Tier 3, gated integration-tests, single-example, real serve boot. Mirrors the ADR-0078 LastTerminated{} literal-ban clause for MemoryPlan. This step lands FOUR of DWD-09's five dst-lint clauses (--disk / --landlock-rules / --seccomp / MemoryPlan-literal-ban). The fifth — the exit observer's loop body contains exactly one release_supervision call, outside match outcome — lands in step 02-02, which is where the observer's release-on-every-arm shape is actually built; this step runs before that call site exists (DWD-09, brief §113).

phases.name: VmReclamation — SD-1's Bar-2 reconciler (cross-cutting, depends on Phase 01's driver)

steps.name: VmHostState port + adapters + VmReclamation reconciler skeleton (plan_reclamation, SupervisionSet)
steps.description: The host-observation driven port (observe/kill_scope/discard_artifacts), its two adapters, and the registered VmReclamation reconciler whose diff is a pure function taking no port.
criteria: plan_reclamation(desired, actual) matches the six-row decision table for every generated VmReclamationState pair; the function takes no port parameter.
Every terminal AllocStatusRow the design's three Ending Classes can produce belongs to exactly one class, never zero, never two.
SupervisionSet::reclamation_authorised is the sole kill-authorising predicate: Unavailable always returns false; Observed(held) returns true iff the alloc is not a member.
RealVmHostState and SimVmHostState are observably equivalent across probe/observe/kill_scope/discard_artifacts, including kill_scope's rmdir-settled-before-return postcondition.
steps.implementation_notes: TEST PARADIGM: Tier 1 pure-function proptest for plan_reclamation/SupervisionSet (mandatory mutation targets, brief.md §113); Tier 3 single-example (@example) for vm_host_state_equivalence.rs. UNSKIP the 3 existing vm_reclamation_plan_purity.rs scaffolds (S-VM-31/32/92) — real bodies per ADR-0083 §D7/brief §105a.1-105a.4. VmReclamationView is FIELD-LESS (ADR-0079 pattern) — needs #[expect(clippy::zero_sized_map_values, ...)] on its bulk-load arm. Wires into the five compiler-enforced sites (AnyReconciler/AnyState/AnyReconcilerView/the 4-tuple match/hydrate_desired/hydrate_actual — brief §105a.9).

steps.name: Authorship claim lifecycle — VmSupervision phases, abandonment boundary, hydration read order, sweep + boot-epoch ordering
steps.description: The Held→EndingInFlight claim sum type, its release on every RetryOutcome arm, hydrate_actual's observe()-first/supervision-last read order, the 30s sweep submission, and the boot-epoch drive's settle-before-adopt ordering.
criteria: The claim releases on all three RetryOutcome arms (Wrote/Failed/NoPriorRow), never only Wrote; release_supervision converges to absent under any interleaving of the observer's and a shim arm's release.
hydrate_actual reads VmHostState::observe() first and the supervision set last; a VM starting between the two reads is never reclaimed.
vm_reclamation_boot::converge runs immediately before adopt_on_restart_recovery; adopt never refuses the boot on a scope the drive already reclaimed.
A node with no Vm registry entry (CH uninstalled) still reclaims its VM survivors via Observed(∅).

dst-lint rejects an exit-observer loop body containing more than one release_supervision call, or one placed inside match outcome — the structural regression guard against release-only-on-Wrote (the SD-1 unreclaimable-orphan shape NEW-1 fixed), landing in the same commit as this step's release-on-every-arm logic (brief §113, DWD-09; the fifth dst-lint clause step 01-10 deliberately deferred here).
steps.implementation_notes: TEST PARADIGM: S-VM-77 is Tier 1 proptest over the transition table (mandatory mutation target — a mutation that ignores transition 3's atomic verdict re-opens NEW-3). S-VM-78 is Tier 1 component-scope, scheduling two hydrate_actual reads with a VM start interleaved between them — its implementation site is reconciler_runtime.rs's hydrate_actual arm (wired at step 02-01), which is why that file is in this step's source scope even though 02-01 built its skeleton. S-VM-23/30 are Tier 3, gated integration-tests, real serve boot with N surviving scopes. Extend vm_reclamation_plan_purity.rs OR a new sibling vm_reclamation_claim_lifecycle.rs — DELIVER's own call per DWD-04. Transition 3 (Held→EndingInFlight) is a check-and-act; its discarded return is the 'Check-and-act must be atomic' defect (development.md). The dst-lint clause (criterion 5) is EXEMPT FROM PARADIGM — static-analysis AST-scanner unit test in xtask, following the existing CrashObservabilityStructLiteral clause shape.

steps.name: The two reclamation executors — write-time terminality guard, four evaluations, disposal's empty universe
steps.description: execute_reclaim_allocation's re-read gates the whole executor (not just the workload_id lookup) and submits the same four evaluations the exit observer submits; execute_discard_stranded_artifacts writes no row and submits none.
criteria: A stopped VM whose scope removal is made to fail is reclaimed by a later tick's steady-state sweep, without restarting serve.
A live VMM whose allocation row is already terminal is killed at tick N; its process, scope, run directory and clone are all gone after the sweep.
A race-losing ReclaimAllocation (the row went terminal before the re-read resolves) is a total no-op: no kill, no discard, no row write, Ok(()), a vm.reclamation.refused event.
Both a restart-orphan and a failed-stop-orphan leave alloc_status[alloc_id] BYTE-UNCHANGED after the kill, including updated_at, last_terminated, restart_count.
Reclaiming an SVID-holding allocation submits a fourth evaluation (svid_lifecycle) alongside the existing three; DropSvid fires and the node drops the leaf private key.
steps.implementation_notes: TEST PARADIGM: Tier 3, gated integration-tests, real serve convergence loop (S-VM-21/22's in-memory companion is already covered by 02-01's plan_reclamation property; this step is their Tier-3 shape). S-VM-79's guard is a mandatory mutation target — a mutant flipping is_terminal there re-opens the NEW-1 residual gap. execute_discard_stranded_artifacts takes NO ObservationStore and NO broker parameter — that absence is structural, not a code-review reminder (DD-5).

steps.name: Sibling-reconciler reclamation guards + P2 property + the four VmReclamation ESR invariants
steps.description: is_natural_exit/the backoff ceiling/startup_probe_failed_action all exempt a reclaimed row; P2 ranges over VmReclamation's own diff; the four DST invariants close the safety/liveness/stability specification.
criteria: A reclaimed Job-kind VM is re-driven by the restart branch, never finalised via FinalizeFailed{Failed{exit_code:Some(0)}}.
Six consecutive serve-restart reclamations never trip RestartBudgetExhausted; the ceiling guard and startup_probe_failed_action both exempt a platform-reclaimed row.
A reclaim-then-restart cycle populates restart_count and last_terminated together, in one scenario.
For any VmReclamationState pair where an alloc is already platform-reclaimed, plan_reclamation's output contains no FinalizeFailed and no StopAllocation{terminal:Some(_)} for it.
The four Invariant variants (VmReclamationConverges, SupervisedVmSurvivesEveryTick, VmReclamationIdempotentSteadyState, EndingInFlightIsNeverReclaimed) all hold under cargo dst.

The cargo dst run demonstrably produces the EndingInFlight window at least once, via a named schedule/seed (a scripted crash-then-observer-delay fault injection, not merely 'the invariant never observed false') — SupervisedVmSurvivesEveryTick is vacuously satisfied exactly at this window (brief §105a.11), so the run must show EndingInFlightIsNeverReclaimed actually witnessing it. A mutant that moves the release point from after the terminal-row write to at process death (or at the watcher's own return) is killed by this DST run.
steps.implementation_notes: TEST PARADIGM: S-VM-26/27/29 are Tier 1 in-memory proptests over WorkloadLifecycle/ServiceLifecycle (mandatory mutation targets); S-VM-28 is Tier 3 single-example; S-VM-80 is Tier 1 proptest directly over VmReclamation (the missing third leg beside the two sibling-reconciler examples); S-VM-24/87/88/89 are Tier 1 DST invariants (assert_always!/assert_eventually!, SimVmHostState + SimClock advancing the 30s cadence deterministically). is_natural_exit is the ONLY predicate whose meaning changes; is_intentionally_stopped/is_restartable need no edit. Criterion 6's demonstrable-window requirement closes the gap where the ESR gate could pass nominally (four invariants never firing false) without the DST harness ever actually exercising the interval EndingInFlightIsNeverReclaimed exists to witness.

steps.name: classify_driver_failure gains a VM arm — kernel/rootfs not found, hypervisor absent, boot deadline, kernel format
steps.description: Cash classify_driver_failure's documented-but-unused DriverType parameter with five Slice-02 Cause variants; zero exec test cases move.
criteria: A deploy whose kernel path does not exist is Failed/VmKernelNotFound naming the exact path, distinct from a missing rootfs.
A deploy whose rootfs path does not exist is Failed/VmRootfsNotFound naming the exact path.
cloud-hypervisor removed after admission but before this allocation's start is Failed/VmHypervisorAbsent naming the paths searched (the TOCTOU window S-VM-12's boot-time gate does not close).
A guest that hangs during boot is Failed/VmBootDeadlineExceeded naming the deadline in ms and the captured console tail; the allocation never passes through Running.

A kernel that exists but is the wrong format for this hypervisor (e.g. a UKI-wrapped image where cloud-hypervisor requires a raw PE Image on aarch64) is Failed/VmKernelFormatUnsupported naming the exact path and arch, worded honestly as a format problem — never CH's misleading firmware-size-cap framing — and distinct from VmKernelNotFound (S-VM-41).
steps.implementation_notes: TEST PARADIGM: Tier 3, gated integration-tests, single-example (five deliberately-broken deploys). Author the RED scaffold fresh at this slice's own RED phase (DWD-06a) — file name is DELIVER's own call within the overdrive-cli/tests/integration/vm_*.rs family DWD-04 commits. classify_driver_failure branches on DriverType FIRST; the exec prefix table is reached only under Exec — zero exec test cases may change (learning hypothesis, slice-02.md). S-VM-41 (DWD-14, closing the ADR-0083 §D5 row-5 VmKernelFormatUnsupported gap a fable review surfaced against this exact step) is the classification-join half of C-7 — companion to S-VM-17's pure-function half (step 01-01, KernelImage::validate rejecting the bad magic before any hypervisor process spawns). This step's classify_driver_failure VM arm maps the resulting KernelFormatError onto TransitionReason::VmKernelFormatUnsupported{path, arch, detail} (ADR-0082 §D2.4, ADR-0083 §D5 row 5); assert on the rendered cause text via workload describe, never on the enum discriminant alone (DWD-14's own acceptance line). The emit-inventory table (ADR-0083 §D5, opening text) separately lacks two rows this step's own scope only touches tangentially — MtlsInterceptInstallFailed and WorkloadNetnsProvisionFailed are absent from the pre-existing 15-row table (17 variants exist); out of this step's scope to backfill (they predate this feature), noted here only so this step's classify_driver_failure work is not mistaken for closing that separate gap too.

steps.name: Unclassified-failure fallthrough — verbatim cause, labelled unclassified
steps.description: A hypervisor failure with no named variant carries CH's verbatim text and is honestly labelled unclassified, using the existing DriverInternalError fallthrough — no new variant minted.
criteria: A VM start failure the platform has no named variant for reports the verbatim hypervisor error text in detail.
The reason is labelled unclassified rather than presented as a known cause.
The fallthrough reuses the EXISTING TransitionReason::DriverInternalError{detail} variant; no new variant is added for this case.
steps.implementation_notes: TEST PARADIGM: Tier 3, gated integration-tests, single-example. Per development.md 'Distinct failure modes get distinct error variants' — this is the deliberate exception: an unclassified failure stays unclassified rather than inventing a variant. The kernel-format case (C-7) is explicitly NOT this scenario — it is caught pre-boot by KernelImage::validate (01-01) and, at the classification layer, by VmKernelFormatUnsupported (03-01, S-VM-41) — and never reaches this fallthrough.

steps.name: [vm] + [service] rejected at deploy time
steps.description: A spec declaring both [vm] and [service] is rejected before scheduling, naming guest networking, guest probes, and guest-stack mTLS interception as missing, citing GH #257 and #222.
criteria: A spec declaring both [service] and [vm] is rejected before anything is scheduled; no intent is committed and no allocation is created.
The rejection message names guest networking, guest-reachable probes, and guest-stack mTLS interception as missing capabilities.
The message cites GH #257 (tap-in-netns + guest probes) and GH #222 (guest-stack mTLS intercept) by number.
steps.implementation_notes: TEST PARADIGM: Tier 3, gated integration-tests, single-example (in-process rejection, no VMM needed). Mirrors the existing ParseError::ProbesNotAllowedOnKind precedent (workload_spec.rs:827) — a semantic rejection with guidance, not a parse error. GH #257 and #222 are real, already-filed issues; do not invent a third.

steps.name: [vm] + [job] / [vm] + [schedule] accepted and run
steps.description: The complementary positive cases: VM job and scheduled-VM specs are accepted and scheduled with no new capability check blocking them.
criteria: A spec declaring [job] + [vm] is accepted and scheduled.
A spec declaring [schedule] (cron) + [vm] is accepted and scheduled.
steps.implementation_notes: TEST PARADIGM: Tier 3, gated integration-tests, single-example. These are the regression guard that 03-03's rejection is scoped to [service] only — [job]/[schedule] combinations must not regress.

phases.name: Stop, restart, VMM death, and confinement (Slice 03)

steps.name: Exit classification — guest-authoritative ExitKind
steps.description: CleanExit comes only from an agent-reported guest exit status; an unreported VMM death or host OOM-kill is Crashed with the same restart/backoff treatment as any process crash.
criteria: A guest kernel panic (hypervisor exits 0) is Failed/VmGuestExitUnreported, never Terminated/Completed.
A host-OOM-killed hypervisor is Failed with the same restart/backoff treatment (same reconciler, same ceiling, same backoff curve) as a crashed process.
Only an agent-reported EXIT 0 produces Terminated/Completed{exit_code:0}.
An operator stop yields intentional_stop:true and consumes no restart budget; it is never counted as a crash.
steps.implementation_notes: TEST PARADIGM: Tier 3, gated integration-tests, single-example. S-VM-42 is a mandatory mutation target (K1 north star) — a mutation collapsing the unreported-death arm into CleanExit must be killed. No code path may derive ExitKind from cloud-hypervisor's own exit status (already enforced structurally by 01-07; this step is its operator-facing Tier-3 proof).

steps.name: Graceful shutdown — overdrive job stop sequencing and bounded grace
steps.description: The operator stop verb writes SHUTDOWN on the beacon connection before any hard kill; an unresponsive guest is still terminated within the bounded grace period.
criteria: overdrive job stop writes SHUTDOWN on the already-open beacon connection before Vmm::terminate is called.
The allocation reaches Terminated/Stopped{Operator} within VM_SHUTDOWN_REQUEST_DEADLINE (2s) + VM_STOP_GRACE (10s).
A guest that ignores the shutdown byte is escalated to Vmm::terminate at the 2s deadline and is never classified a crash.
steps.implementation_notes: TEST PARADIGM: Tier 3, gated integration-tests, single-example. This is the FIRST real evidence for the host→guest SHUTDOWN write — the spike exercised the vsock connection guest→host only (findings.md:2787); treat as a mechanism proof, not a regression guard (ADR-0082 §D4). The pre-beacon-stop and already-dead-VMM edge cases are already covered component-scope by 01-07's S-VM-76 — this step is their Tier-3 operator-facing companion for the responsive/unresponsive-guest cases only.

steps.name: Restart from a clean rootfs copy
steps.description: A crash-restarted VM boots from a fresh FICLONE copy of the operator's rootfs; the original artifact is never mutated.
criteria: A VM workload that crashed after modifying its rootfs is restarted under backoff and boots from an unmodified copy of the operator's original artifact.
The operator's artifact file on the host is byte-unchanged before and after the crash-restart cycle.
steps.implementation_notes: TEST PARADIGM: Tier 3, gated integration-tests, single-example. Reuses 01-06's FICLONE mechanism verbatim — this step proves the RESTART path re-invokes create() with a fresh clone rather than reusing a mutated one.

steps.name: Hypervisor confinement — Landlock/uid-drop/rlimits on the spawned process
steps.description: The running VM's hypervisor is a bounded, non-root, Landlock-confined process whose ruleset follows the operator's declared artifact paths.
criteria: /proc/<vmm-pid>/status reports non-zero real and effective Uid/Gid; /proc/<vmm-pid>/limits reports Max-file-size and Max-open-files strictly below the same fields on overdrive serve's own process.
The Landlock ruleset names CH's auto-derived grants (kernel/disk/serial/api-socket) plus a read-write grant on the run directory, and nothing outside those.
A rootfs declared outside the default artifact directory still boots and is reachable — the ruleset is derived from the spec, never hardcoded.
The run directory holds nothing but this VM's own sockets and logs; the vsock socket's Landlock grant is the containing directory, since CH does not auto-derive one for it.
steps.implementation_notes: TEST PARADIGM: Tier 3, gated integration-tests, single-example, PID resolution via the allocation's cgroup scope cgroup.procs (never a driver-internal handle). Landlock grant derivation (VmRunDir::landlock_rules, ADR-0082 §D2.2) already lands in 01-01/01-06; this step is the real-boot proof. The vsock-directory-grant clause is a dst-lint target too (01-10) — this AT is its behavioral complement (brief.md §113).

steps.name: Confinement fail-closed + no new operator surface
steps.description: A host that cannot supply required confinement refuses the workload rather than starting it degraded; confinement adds nothing to the deploy surface an operator sees.
criteria: A host that cannot supply a required ConfinementControl (e.g. no --landlock below the version floor) is Failed/VmConfinementUnavailable naming the unavailable control; the hypervisor is never started unconfined.
The unavailable-confinement condition is injected at the Vmm port boundary via SimVmm (system constraint 1); no genuinely Landlock-less host exists in the Lima test envelope.
Confinement adds no new deploy flag, table, or verb; the terminal state and exit code an operator reads are unchanged from Slice 01.
steps.implementation_notes: TEST PARADIGM: Tier 3, gated integration-tests, single-example, using the SAME ServerConfig.vmm_override seam 01-09 wired (ADR-0083 §D8) — do not invent a second injection mechanism. Mandatory mutation target: warn-and-continue must be killed (the fail-closed arm).

phases.name: Volumes and the storage daemon's honesty (Slice 04)

steps.name: [[vm.volume]] spec parse + VmConfig volume payload + derived shared=on + no-volume regression guard
steps.description: The volume array-of-tables surface, the derived --memory shared=on flag, and the guard proving a volume-free VM is byte-identical to Slices 01-03.
criteria: A VM job with no volume declared starts no storage daemon, derives shared=on OFF, and reaches the same terminal state and exit code as before volumes existed.
An unrecognised [[vm.volume]] key (e.g. "cache") is rejected by name; only source, target and read_only are accepted.
shared=on is derived from !volumes.is_empty() at one VmConfig construction site — no builder, no second config shape.
steps.implementation_notes: TEST PARADIGM: S-VM-57 is Tier 3, gated integration-tests, single-example (the regression guard); S-VM-62 is Tier 1 in-memory (parse rejection, no VMM). Author fresh at Slice 04's own RED phase (DWD-06a). [[vm.volume]] rides inside Slice 01's JobEnvelope V2 (01-02) — no second rkyv bump. S-VM-62 lands in the EXISTING vm_spec_driver_table_dispatch.rs (created at step 01-08, DWD-04's parse-boundary-rejection placement — same file as S-VM-06/07), not a CLI integration file; do not create a redundant Tier-3 CLI test for it.

steps.name: Supervised virtiofsd lifecycle — ordering, socket readiness, teardown
steps.description: One supervised virtiofsd per volume-carrying VM, in the allocation's cgroup scope and netns, running before the guest boots and torn down after the VM.
criteria: A missing virtiofsd binary is Failed/VmStorageDaemonAbsent naming the paths searched, distinct from a missing source directory.
The guest does not begin booting until the storage daemon's socket is ready; an expired readiness wait is Failed/VmStorageSocketTimeout naming the socket and the wait.
No daemon process or vhost-user socket survives any terminal path — a failed start, a readiness timeout, or a sandbox refusal.
steps.implementation_notes: TEST PARADIGM: Tier 3, gated integration-tests, single-example. virtiofsd is a sidecar VmDriver spawns and supervises DIRECTLY (Command::spawn, same shape as ExecDriver's own workload process) — it sits OUTSIDE the Vmm port entirely (system constraint 9). Placement: allocation's cgroup scope + netns (load-bearing — cgroup_kill must reap it). overdrive-host/src/virtiofsd.rs is NOT a port/trait seam — no storage-daemon supervision port is minted (ADR-0083 §D8, explicit ruling: 'Path (a) is explicitly not taken'). It holds plain spawn/supervise helper functions (Command::spawn + wait, mirroring ExecDriver's own workload-process handling) that VmDriver (overdrive-worker, which already depends on overdrive-host per Cargo.toml) calls directly. Do not treat it as a trait boundary or add a Vmm-shaped abstraction over it.

steps.name: Host<->guest byte-faithful round-trip + read-only host-side enforcement
steps.description: A guest write inside a declared volume is byte-identical on the host, read by ordinary filesystem access; a read-only volume defeats even an uncooperative guest.
criteria: A guest write inside a declared volume is present, readable, and byte-identical in the operator's host source directory, verified by ordinary filesystem access, not through any Overdrive API.
A read_only=true volume's guest write fails inside the guest and the host directory is byte-unchanged, including against a guest that tries to remount the share read-write.
A missing volume source directory is Failed/VmVolumeSourceNotFound naming the source and the path, distinct from a missing rootfs and a missing storage daemon.
steps.implementation_notes: TEST PARADIGM: Tier 3, gated integration-tests, single-example. S-VM-56 is a mandatory mutation target and MUST defeat a guest-side-only implementation — a cooperative guest's failed write alone is insufficient evidence (US-VM-8 AC 2). read_only is enforced HOST-side (the export); a guest-side -o ro is an ergonomic guard only, never the boundary. virtiofsd.rs (overdrive-host) is plain spawn/supervise helpers, not a port trait — see 05-02's note; this step's host<->guest byte-faithful assertions read/write the operator's source directory directly via ordinary filesystem access, never through a (nonexistent) storage-daemon port.

steps.name: Guest-side mount + refuse-to-exec (the composite-lie case) + Landlock non-widening
steps.description: overdrive-init refuses to exec the operator's command when a required mount fails; a volume never widens what the hypervisor process can reach.
criteria: overdrive-init refuses to exec the operator's command when a required volume mount fails; the allocation is Failed/VmGuestMountFailed naming the volume that could not be mounted.
The allocation with a failed required mount NEVER reaches a completed terminal state — never Terminated/Completed{exit_code:0} over an empty host directory.

The volume source directory never appears in the hypervisor's Landlock ruleset for a volume-carrying allocation; the rest of the [D7] posture (uid, rlimits, cgroup, netns) is unchanged from a volume-free VM on the SAME allocation.
steps.implementation_notes: TEST PARADIGM: Tier 3, gated integration-tests, single-example. S-VM-60 is THE mandatory mutation target the [D4] amendment exists to defend — without the refuse-to-exec guard, the command writes into the discarded per-launch rootfs copy, exits 0, and workload describe lies. overdrive-init's fifth duty (mount then refuse) is a scoped, non-passive amendment — name the subject, per the [D8g] correction.

steps.name: RLIMIT_FSIZE accounts for shared=on's memfd + storage-daemon sandbox launch-argument
steps.description: rlimit_fsize() covers a memfd-backed guest uniformly; the storage daemon's launch argument is a pure rendering-site value that only ever emits --sandbox=namespace or a typed refusal.
criteria: rlimit_fsize() always returns max(rootfs image size, guest RAM), uniformly whether or not shared=on is in play for this VmConfig.
The storage daemon's launch-argument rendering always emits --sandbox=namespace for an available capability signal.
An unavailable capability signal always yields a typed refusal, never a launch; no input ever yields --sandbox=chroot and no input ever omits --sandbox.
steps.implementation_notes: TEST PARADIGM: Tier 1, default lane, proptest, both mandatory mutation targets. S-VM-67's driving port is a value with private fields and exactly one rendering site (mirroring DiskAttachment::to_disk_arg's D2.1 shape) — the exact type is NOT yet ADR-pinned; DELIVER names it at RED phase per CLAUDE.md 'Implement to the design' (do not invent a storage-daemon supervision port — ADR-0083 §D8 explicitly mints none). The rendering type ITSELF lands in overdrive-core (crates/overdrive-core/src/vm/config.rs), mirroring the DiskAttachment §D2.1 precedent — private fields, one rendering site, pure, testable in this step's own overdrive-core acceptance file. overdrive-host is never a dev-dependency of overdrive-core's test lane (development.md § 'Port-trait dependencies'), so the rendering type cannot live in overdrive-host; only the impure spawn call site that consumes the rendered value lives in overdrive-host/src/virtiofsd.rs (or wherever 05-02 places the virtiofsd module). S-VM-67's Then proves ONLY the rendered argument; it does NOT prove a running virtiofsd enforces the sandbox or that the platform fails closed end-to-end — that stays an undischarged Tier-3 property of this slice (DWD-13), not covered by any scenario in this roadmap.

steps.name: Storage-daemon exit honesty — clean exit contributes nothing, mid-run death is never clean
steps.description: The daemon's own exit status never drives ExitKind in either direction; a mid-run death overrides even a guest-reported clean exit.
criteria: A completed VM job's storage-daemon exit is observed in the allocation's event/audit trail while contributing nothing to ExitKind.
A storage daemon that dies while the guest is still running is Failed/VmStorageDaemonDied naming the socket, never Terminated/Completed; disposition StoppedBy::Process, never PlatformReclaimed.
A guest that self-reports EXIT 0 over vsock AFTER its storage daemon already died still resolves VmStorageDaemonDied, overriding the guest-reported clean exit.
steps.implementation_notes: TEST PARADIGM: Tier 3, gated integration-tests, single-example, both shapes of S-VM-65 mandatory. The exit_observer's storage_daemon_died precedence check runs AHEAD of ExitKind entirely — NOT nested inside the Crashed arm the way VmOutOfMemory (row 13) is (ADR-0083 §D5 row 14). S-VM-64 must discriminate, not merely observe green: assert the daemon's exit WAS observed while contributing nothing — a do-nothing implementation would also pass a naive assertion.

steps.name: vCPU derivation from cpu_milli — rounding + floor of 1
steps.description: The vCPU-derivation pure function rounds up and floors at one; the guest-observed CPU count matches the declared figure.
criteria: Declared cpu_milli=2000 yields exactly two guest-observed online CPUs, observed from inside the guest, never asserted against the constructed hypervisor config.
A sub-core request (cpu_milli=250) still yields exactly one online CPU and the allocation reaches Running.
vCPU derivation is max(1, round_up(cpu_milli/1000)) for any u32 including 0 and non-multiples of 1000; the result is never zero.
steps.implementation_notes: TEST PARADIGM: S-VM-73 is Tier 1 default-lane proptest, mandatory mutation target — author fresh (name pinned by DELIVER's own DESIGN reading, per US-VM-5 Technical Notes; the derivation rule itself is DESIGN's). S-VM-69/70 are Tier 3, gated integration-tests, single-example, real guest CPU count read, which needs a real DriverRegistry-composed serve (step 01-08).

steps.name: Guest memory sizing matches the declared figure
steps.description: The declared memory_bytes is what the guest observes; workload describe reports the same figure for a VM allocation as for a process allocation.
criteria: Declared memory_bytes=2147483648 yields approximately 2 GiB of memory observed inside the guest.
overdrive workload describe reports the same declared memory_bytes figure for a VM allocation as it already does for a process allocation.
steps.implementation_notes: TEST PARADIGM: Tier 3, gated integration-tests, single-example, real boot, assertion taken from inside the guest — never from the hypervisor config the platform generated (asserting on generated config would only prove we wrote what we wrote).

steps.name: Sizing parity across both memory backings + Driver::resize
steps.description: Guest-observed vCPU/memory match the declared figures identically on private memory and on shared=on; resize rejects with a named, typed reason (hotplug is GH #92's right-sizing reconciler, out of this feature's scope), never a silent no-op.
criteria: One parametrized Tier-3 case: guest-observed vCPU count and memory size match the declared figures identically for a volume-free (private memory) and a volume-carrying (shared=on) VM.

Driver::resize rejects every call with a named, typed reason citing GH #92 as the deferred hotplug work (ADR-0082 §D4: the api-socket 'is not depended on by any path in this feature'); it never silently no-ops and never hotplugs in this feature.
steps.implementation_notes: TEST PARADIGM: Tier 3, gated integration-tests, single parametrized case (not two separate tests) — the reason Slice 04 (volumes) is ordered before Slice 05 (resources). Driver::resize rejects, always — ADR-0082 §D4 keeps --api-socket in VmConfig only as the future hotplug substrate for GH #92's right-sizing reconciler and states plainly it 'is not depended on by any path in this feature'; a silent no-op is a review rejection, and so is an implemented hotplug this feature does not need.
